contexts.text: By the bath and by the hin were measured the liquids which served as drink; hence by these measures truths are signified; the containant takes this signification from the thing contained.
The ephah and the hin were measures, and measures = the quantity of the thing treated of... a hin which was a measure of wine and oil, the quantity of truth. ().
A hin () = the amount of the conjunction. A hin, which was a measure of liquids, here, of oil, = the amount of the conjunction...

Two measures which were in sacred use are mentioned in the Word, one for liquids, which is called a hin... By the hin were measured oil and wine... The measure hin... was divided into four... in order that it might signify what is conjunctive. AC 10262:3, Illustrated.

As by a hin is also signified the amount of the conjunction with spiritual truth... there was taken for the meat-offering in the sacrifices of a ram the third part of a hin of oil, and for the drink-offering a third part of wine ().
